title: Correct work value
description: Essential: The response must state the work done by the athlete as 4.5 J (or equivalent with correct units).

title: Correct force magnitude
description: Essential: The response must state the magnitude of the applied force as 9 N (or equivalent with correct units).

title: Energy ratio application
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply the constant ratio of kinetic energy before and after ground collisions to both scenarios.

title: Work-energy setup
description: Important: The solution must set up work-energy relationships for both the free-fall and athlete-assisted scenarios.

title: Athlete's work calculation
description: Important: The solution must correctly calculate the athlete's work using either the energy difference or the force × displacement method.

title: Force from kinematics
description: Optional: The solution may derive the applied force using kinematics (displacement during force application) and Newton's second law.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All intermediate and final answers should maintain consistent units (J, N, m, kg, s).

title: Sign error in work
description: Pitfall: Incorrect sign for the athlete's work (should be positive as energy is added to the ball).

title: Ignoring gravity in force
description: Pitfall: Calculating the applied force without accounting for gravity (F_net = F_applied + mg, not just F_applied).

title: Energy ratio confusion
description: Pitfall: Misapplying the kinetic energy ratio (e.g., using potential energy heights directly without converting to kinetic energy).
